• alef-dual-ml-alef-first — words with two vowel letters in a row, alef first: alef-vav for ḥolam or shuruq, alef-yod for ḥiriq
  • alef-dual-ml-alef-second — words with two vowel letters in a row, alef second: a ḥolam male or a shuruq followed by a quiescent alef
  • dexi-stress-meteg — chanted words in which the letter with deḥi's stress helper also has a meteg, each with MAM's documentation note on it
  • doc-note-notation — words in MAM's documentation notes written in plus notation or with a carrier letter between double guillemets
  • holam-before-vav — a ḥolam dot on a letter other than vav just before a vav, grouped by whether the vav has a mark above it
  • kq-complex — ketiv/qere cases identified from their context: qere before ketiv after a narrow-sense paseq or before sof pasuq, and two or three cases in a row
  • kq-simple — ketiv/qere cases identified from their template and its immediate surroundings, grouped by their numbers of ketiv and qere words
  • mtgmtg — chanted words with two or more Unicode METEG marks, counting any silluq, grouped by the presence of sof pasuq and of maqaf
  • oleh-yored — oleh-weyored, grouped by where its oleh and yored are: on one letter, in one atom, in one chanted word, or in separate chanted words
  • pasoleg-1 — munaḥ legarmeh, and munaḥ followed by a narrow-sense paseq, grouped by the accent that ends the pattern and the accents in between
  • pasoleg-2 — legarmeh and narrow-sense paseq marks, alone or in runs over two or three consecutive chanted words
  • poetic-stress-helpers — places where MAM's template for deḥi's stress helper is inside another template or holds one, and tsinnor's forms with its stress helper
  • poetic-verlen — poetic verses grouped by their length in chanted words
  • qamats-variants — words that MAM has in two forms, one with qamats qatan where the other has plain qamats
  • quick-brown-fox — pangram-like verses, with an unusually wide variety of letters, final-form letters, vowel points or stress helpers
  • rare-tmpls — verses with one of MAM's rare templates, such as the inverted nun, the scroll-difference note and the “good ending”
  • revia-mugrash — chanted words in poetic verses whose revia mugrash has its geresh muqdam and its revia on one letter
  • sec-merk — chanted words with merkha and another accent or a meteg, grouped by the pattern of their accents, maqaf marks and meteg marks
  • sec-merk-shewa — the sec-merk chanted words whose merkha is followed by a letter with shewa or a ḥataf vowel, grouped by that letter's marks
  • sec-misc — chanted words grouped as in sec-merk, but with mahapakh, or tarḥa in a poetic verse, instead of merkha
  • sec-misc-shewa — the sec-misc chanted words whose mahapakh is followed by a letter with shewa or a ḥataf vowel, grouped by that letter's marks
  • sec-star-breuer-cos — the sec-merk and sec-misc chanted words again, grouped by the passage of Breuer's CoS cited for each
  • slh-word — words with a small, large or hung letter, grouped three ways: by the number of such letters, by context, and by kind
  • tsinnorit — chanted words with tsinnorit, grouped by the accents, maqaf marks and meteg marks after the tsinnorit, or before it
  • unicode — unusual characters and mark sequences, such as varika, rafeh, alef with mapiq, the extraordinary dots, and ḥataf vowels on non-guttural letters
  • xataf-qamats — chanted words with ḥataf qamats, each with the letter that has it
